name: ELEGANT V (NaI dark matter detector)
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

ELEGANT V is recorded for its NaI dark matter detector only; the experiment also searched for double beta decay of 100Mo (RCNP group page: '100Mo source of double beta decay'), which is not recorded here. The sister detector ELEGANT VI (25 CaF2 scintillators, Oto, from November 1997; WIMP and 48Ca double-beta aims) is not recorded: its published results read are double-beta results and no dark matter paper was found.

No result record: ELEGANT V's dark matter limits and annual modulation search were published in journals whose abstracts could not be read (APS returned 403); they are described only in secondary text: 'A search for annual modulation did not show any indication of modulation.' (arXiv:astro-ph/0112550, a 2002 overview) and shown as the 'ELEGANT V at OTO' curve in arXiv:astro-ph/0506329. Tier C.

Two periods: nine NaI modules (central 36.5 kg detector) at Kamioka from 1992 (arXiv:2607.24448, which cites Phys. Rev. C 47, R425 (1993)) and 16 modules (0.76 tons) at Oto from April 1997; the sources do not say when the Kamioka configuration ended: the end 1997-04 of the Kamioka prototype-host role and placement is inferred (uncertain), the interval has no end.
The PICO-LON project later reused ELEGANT V's old lead shield (arXiv:astro-ph/0611700).

summary.plain: ELEGANT V was a 0.76-ton array of sodium iodide crystals in Japan's Oto Cosmo Observatory, an underground laboratory in Nara, used to search for dark matter alongside double-beta-decay studies. Its crystals and lead shield later served the PICO-LON dark matter project.
summary.technical: ELEGANT V (ELEctron GAmma-ray Neutrino Telescope V) at the Oto Cosmo Observatory: 16 NaI(Tl) scintillators (0.76 tons) inside lead and copper shields with drift chambers and plastic scintillators around a 100Mo double-beta source; the NaI array was used for dark matter searches (spin-dependent limits and an annual modulation search per the 2002 overview). An earlier configuration with nine NaI modules (central 36.5 kg detector) was deployed at Kamioka in 1992 (threshold 4 keV, background ~5.1 cpd/kg/keV at 5 keV).
